1st Revised Sheet No. 223-1 Cancels Original Sheet No. 223-1 ... Issued: August 28, 2026 ... Effective: August 28, 2026

contract_term.value: Initial term not less than the Load Ramp Period (not over four years) plus 8 years (12 years with a 4-year ramp); after the initial term, termination or a change of contract capacity on written notice no later than three years ahead

cites.quote: “Load Ramp Period” refers to the time of commencement of service until the customer reaches full contract capacity, which shall not exceed four years.

cites.section: Sheet 223-5, Terms of Contract, New Load
cites.quote: For New Load only, contracts under the Schedule shall be made for an initial period of not less than the Load Ramp Period plus 8 years. By way of example, the initial period of a Contract for a Data Center with a 4-year Load Ramp Period will be 12 years.

After the initial term, Contracts shall remain in effect unless terminated by either party by providing written notice to the other party no later than three (3) years prior to the requested date of termination.

exit_fee.value: During the initial term the customer pays the minimum charges whether it curtails, reduces, suspends or terminates service; after the fifth contract year following the Load Ramp Period it may terminate by paying an exit fee equal to minimum charges for 36 months after notice of termination; up to 25% of contract capacity may be assigned to another DCT customer in lieu of some or all of the exit fee

cites.quote: During the initial term of the Contract, the customer will be financially responsible to pay the minimum charges regardless of the customer choosing to curtail, reduce, suspend, or terminate service. If after completion of the fifth year of the Contract after the Load Ramp Period the customer chooses to pay an exit fee equal to minimum charges for 36 months after notice of termination, the customer can thereafter terminate the contract.

cites.section: Assigning Retail Capacity to Another Customer
cites.quote: it may request that Ohio Power assign up to 25% of its contract capacity to another Schedule DCT customer in lieu of paying some or all of its exit fee associated with the reallocated capacity.

study_timeline.value: Load study fee of $10,000 to $100,000 (by size) paid within 45 days; reasonable efforts to complete the load study within 60 days if regional transmission upgrades are needed, otherwise 45 days; 60 days to sign the LOA and ESA; collateral within 30 days of signing; the next study tranche begins 1 October 2026 for applications received by 30 September 2026

cites.section: Steps for Processing New Service Requests of 25,000 kW or Greater
cites.quote: Ohio Power will charge a one-time fee of $10,000 to $100,000 for each load study to be paid within 45 days.

cites.section: Steps for Processing New Service Requests of 25,000 kW or Greater
cites.quote: will make reasonable efforts to complete a load study within (i) 60 days if regional transmission upgrades are needed to serve the customer; or (ii) 45 days for all other situations.
Customers have 60 days to sign their LOA and ESA.
The next round of studies will commence on October 1, 2026. Applications must be received by September 30, 2026, to be considered for this tranche.
Customers who do sign will be required to provide the collateral specified in the LOA, ESA, and Schedule DCT ... within 30 days of signing.

service to customers under this schedule will not commence until the Company has sufficient capacity to meet the contractual load requirements.

min_demand.value: Monthly billing demand not less than 90% of the greater of contract capacity or the highest billing demand of the past 11 months; the minimum charge also bills Base Billing Energy of 65% of contract capacity times the billing hours

cites.quote: the monthly billing demand so established shall, in no event, be less than 90% of the greater of (a) the customer’s contract capacity, or (b) the customer’s highest previously established monthly billing demand during the past 11 months.
The Base Billing Energy will be computed as follows: Contract Capacity (kW) multiplied by 65% multiplied by Number of Billing Hours in the Month.
a 90% monthly minimum billing demand and 65% monthly minimum energy requirement

contract_term.value: Initial Contract Term not less than 15 years, after an optional Load Ramp Period of up to five years; at least 60 months' written notice to terminate; automatic five-year renewals after the Contract Term

cites.quote: The Large Load Customer’s Initial Contract Term will be made for a period of not less than 15 years. A Large Load Customer may designate a Load Ramp Period, which can be no greater than five (5) years.
Either party shall give at least 60 months written notice to the other party of the intention to terminate the contract.

At the conclusion of the Contract Term, the contract shall automatically renew in five-year contract extensions unless the Large Load Customer provides 60 months written notice of the intention to terminate the contract.
requiring a contract term of 15 years with a maximum 5-year period to ramp up to its full load

collateral.value: 50% of the Exit Fee, provided within 10 business days of contract signing, recalculated annually or on a material change; standby letter of credit (A-/A3 bank, 360-day minimum term) or cash

cites.quote: The amount of collateral to be provided within 10 business days of contract signing and unless otherwise approved by the Commission, the Large Load Customer shall provide collateral in the amount of 50% of the Exit Fee.
This amount shall be recalculated annually or upon any material change to the contract term or minimum monthly charges.
Such security must be issued for a minimum term of 360 days.

exit_fee.value: Termination, a switch to an AES, or a reduction beyond 10% at any time during the Contract Term on at least 60 months' notice, with an Exit Fee equal to the remaining Minimum Charge for the terminated or reduced capacity for the rest of the Contract Term; a one-time reduction of up to 10% without fee after the first five years on at least 48 months' notice

cites.quote: Large Load Customer may terminate its contract, elect to take service from a qualified AES, or reduce its contract capacity beyond 10% at any time during the Contract Term by giving the Company at least 60 months written notice prior to the beginning of the PJM Delivery Year for which the reduction or termination is sought, subject to payment of a capacity reduction/termination fee (“Exit Fee”). The Exit Fee shall be equal to the remaining Minimum Charge, based on the Large Load Customers total Contract Capacity for the terminated/reduced capacity for the remainder of the Contract Term, unless determined otherwise by the Commission.

Large Load Customer may, without payment of an Exit Fee or any penalty, reduce its contract capacity at any time after the first five (5) years of the Contract Term via a one-time election not to exceed 10%, by giving the Company at least 48 months written notice prior to the beginning of the PJM Delivery Year for which the reduction is sought.

rows.license_basis: The tariff sheets were read only in I&M's Michigan tariff book on indianamichiganpower.com (AEP legal notice: personal use only). The MPSC's release of 27 August 2026 on michigan.gov is public and alone supports the 50 MW threshold, the 15-year term with a five-year ramp, the 90 percent minimum demand and 65 percent minimum energy, the order date and the case number.
rows.notes: The MPSC release says the amendments require '4 years of notice if the customer plans to reduce capacity more than 10%', but the sheet prints at least 48 months for a one-time reduction of up to 10% and at least 60 months for a reduction beyond 10% (Sheet D-39.10): a discrepancy for review. The release also states that I&M must propose a standalone large-load rate in its next general rate case, model six cost allocation and rate designs, and make an ex parte filing before each new customer takes service. The MPSC order itself (e-dockets) was not found in a readable form; ADMS order document 27364 is a different case (U-21682).

cites.quote: so long as that new load or load expansion itself has a contract capacity greater than or equal to 100 MW at an individual site or 150 MW on an aggregated basis

min_demand.value: Monthly billing demand not less than the greater of 80 percent of contract capacity or 80 percent of the highest billing demand of the past 11 months; the minimum charge also bills Base Billing Energy of 60% of contract capacity times the billing hours

cites.quote: The monthly billing demand established hereunder shall not be less than the greater of (a) 80 percent of the Large Load Customer's contract capacity specified for the applicable time period of the Contract Term; or (b) 80 percent of the Large Load Customer's highest previously established Monthly Billing Demand during the past 11 months.

contract_term.value: Initial Contract Term not less than 12 years, after an optional Load Ramp Period of up to five years; reductions or termination after the first five years on at least 42 months' written notice

cites.quote: The Large Load Customer’s Initial Contract Term will be made for a period of not less than 12 years. A Large Load Customer may designate a Load Ramp Period, which can be no greater than five years.

collateral.value: 24 times the previous maximum monthly non-fuel bill (the maximum expected bill in the first contract year), recomputed annually and updated if 10% greater

cites.quote: The amount of collateral provided shall be equal to 24 times the Large Load Customer’s previous maximum monthly non-fuel bill. During the first year of the contract, the maximum expected bill for the year shall be used.

exit_fee.value: Up to 20% reduction without fee after the first five years on 42 months' notice; termination or reduction beyond 20% pays an Exit Fee equal to the nominal value of the remaining Minimum Charge for the capacity above the 20% allowance, over an Exit Fee Period of one to five years

cites.quote: Large Load Customer may, without payment of an Exit Fee or any penalty, reduce its contract capacity at any time after the first five years of the Initial Contract Term by up to 20%, in total, by giving the Companies at least 42 months written notice

The Exit Fee shall be calculated as the nominal value of the remaining Minimum Charge for the terminated/reduced capacity in excess of the 20% allowed reduction for the first year of the Exit Fee Period
The Exit Fee Period shall not be less than one year and shall not exceed five years.

rows.notes: Leads, not verified: the rate case is OCC Cause No. PUD-2025-000075 (OKCFox; that page's robots bar Claude's agents, so it was not read), the ALJ's report was filed 21 August 2026 and recommended approval of the large-load tariff proposal (Tulsa Flyer, 24 August 2026), and the class would cover customers over 75 MW (Tulsa Flyer) while LBNL's August 2026 brief says the proposed Large Power and Light tariff applies above 10 MW; a Southwest Ledger item cites PSO testimony in PUD 2025-000064 that 11 customers of 50 MW or more are under letters of agreement or contracts. Oklahoma's Data Center Customer Ratepayer Protection Act of 2026 (17 O.S. 900 to 906) defines a large load customer at 75 MW or more added after 1 July 2026 (OCC page, read). The OCC order is expected in Q4 2026: status may change soon.
